decisions.reason: Removing the cuts requirement does not alter the independently specified audio-level or mix standards; the source provides no candidate-specific value or scope change.
The subtitle standard is independent of editing cuts, and the source does not change its value or scope.
The opening-hook requirements remain semantically unchanged by removal of the separate cuts requirement.
The selected reference basis and adaptation mode do not depend on retaining the cuts requirement, and the source establishes no replacement reference direction.
The product-benefit and claim rules are independent of editing cuts and contain no cut-related attributes requiring cleanup.
The keyword and wording constraints remain valid unchanged; the source does not address script language or terminology.
Audience age and Indian-market targeting are unaffected by removal of the editing-cuts requirement.
The source does not modify the preview duration, language, content, or approval purpose; shared task context alone does not entail an impact.
The Hindi-only script and dialogue constraints are independent of editing cuts and receive no value or scope change from the source.
The realistic UGC visual standard remains independently meaningful and has no cut-specific attribute made obsolete by the source removal.
Actor nationality and gender preferences are unrelated to the removed cuts requirement and remain unchanged.
The requirement to include both products does not depend on the editing-cuts requirement, and the source provides no product-placement change.
